sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: How should your back, feet, and legs fit the driver's seat before shifting out of park?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: A driver sits upright with back supported, feet resting on the floor, and pedals comfortably reachable.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: How far should your chest sit from the steering wheel, and how high should the wheel top sit?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: A driver keeps about ten inches of space between chest and steering wheel, keeps the seatback upright, and keeps the wheel top at or below shoulder and chin height.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Where should the headrest touch your head, and how should your foot move between the gas and brake?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A driver positions the headrest to touch the back of the head above ear level and moves the foot between pedals with the heel staying on the floor.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: What posture and chest-to-wheel measurement protect you best in the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Sit upright with your back on the seat and keep ten inches between your chest and the steering wheel

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Relative to your shoulders and chin, how high should the top of the steering wheel be adjusted?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Keep the top of the steering wheel at shoulder height or lower and below chin level

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How high on the back of your head should a properly adjusted headrest make contact?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Position the headrest so it touches the back of your head above ear level

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How do you aim the inside rearview mirror and adapt it for daytime versus nighttime glare?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: A driver centers the inside mirror on the rear window and selects the day or night setting to match driving conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How much of your own car's side should appear in properly aimed outside mirrors?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: A driver sets the outside mirrors so only a sliver of the vehicle side shows, widening coverage of neighboring lanes to shrink blind spots from a normal seated position.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How do the inside mirror and two outside mirrors work together when adjusted properly?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Frame the rear window with the inside mirror and set the outside mirrors to barely show each side of the vehicle

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Who must use a seat belt or child restraint, and what three protections do belts provide?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Every person in the vehicle uses a fastened belt or child seat, because belts hold occupants inside, reduce crash injury, and help the driver keep control.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Where must the shoulder strap and lap belt rest on your body, and what two shortcuts are unsafe?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A correctly worn belt has a snug shoulder strap across shoulder and chest plus a lap portion low across the hips, fastened securely and never tucked under the arm or behind the back.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What does Utah's occupant-restraint law mandate for all passengers and for children age eight or younger?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Utah law requires every passenger to buckle up, and every child age eight or younger must ride properly secured in a car or booster seat.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: How many pounds of crash force hit a 150-pound person in a 30 mph impact, and why can't arms brace against it?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Crash forces equal body weight multiplied by vehicle speed, so a one hundred fifty-pound occupant in a thirty miles per hour crash experiences four thousand five hundred pounds of force that cannot be resisted by bracing.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: How are unbuckled-passenger citations counted for a Utah driver, and when does special stop authority kick in?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: A driver who carries an unrestrained passenger can receive one citation for each unrestrained person, with special stop authority when anyone under sixteen is unrestrained.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Where do lap and shoulder straps belong, and where must the shoulder strap never be routed?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Route the lap belt across the hips and the shoulder strap across the shoulder and chest, never under the arm or behind the back

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: At what height may a child age eight or younger graduate out of an approved safety or booster seat in Utah?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Every child age eight or younger must use an approved safety seat unless the child has reached fifty-seven inches in height.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What age, weight, and height milestones guide moving a child from rear-facing to forward-facing to a booster?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Children ride rear-facing in the back seat to at least age two and thirty pounds, then forward-facing with a harness in the back seat to at least age four and forty pounds, then in a booster until the belt fits and they reach fifty-seven inches.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: How must children ages eight through twelve be restrained, and through what age should kids stay in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Children ages eight through twelve must use a suitable restraint or belt, and children age twelve or younger should keep riding in the back seat.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How fast do dashboard airbags inflate, and how do they interact with seat belts?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Air bags supplement belts rather than replacing them, deploy from the dashboard at up to two hundred miles per hour, and protect best when occupants are buckled and children ride restrained in the back.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What strict rule governs infants and passenger airbags, and what if an older child must ride in an airbag seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Infants never ride in front of an active passenger air bag, children twelve and under ride buckled in the rear, and any child who must use an air-bag seat is moved fully rearward and properly secured.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What offense classes apply in Utah to disabling an airbag versus smoking in a car carrying children 15 or younger?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Disabling or failing to repair a vehicle air-bag system is a Class B misdemeanor, and smoking in a vehicle carrying children age fifteen or younger is an infraction when stopped.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Which young passengers require an approved safety seat unless they reach 57 inches?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Secure every child eight years old or younger in an approved safety seat unless the child is fifty-seven inches tall

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Until what minimum age and weight should a young child remain rear-facing in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Keep a child rear-facing in the back seat until at least two years of age and thirty pounds

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: Until what minimum age and weight should a child ride forward-facing in a five-point harness in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Keep a child forward-facing with a harness in the back seat until at least four years of age and forty pounds

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Once a child outgrows a 40-pound harness, how long must they keep riding in a belt-positioning booster?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Move a child weighing about forty pounds into a booster seat until the adult belt fits and the child is fifty-seven inches tall

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: How should every driver treat airbags alongside seat belts and infant carriers?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Treat an air bag as a high-speed device that works with safety belts, and never place an infant in front of a passenger air bag

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: How should your hands grip the steering wheel, and which way do you turn it moving forward or backward?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: The driver keeps both hands on the outside of the wheel, grips with fingers rather than palms, and turns the wheel toward the intended travel direction in forward or reverse.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What gear, pedal, and instrument checks belong right before putting your vehicle in motion?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: A driver begins with the selector in park or the clutch engaged and the brake held, then checks lamps and gauges before moving.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How should you position your body and steer when backing up, and on which highways is reversing illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: When backing, the driver looks through the rear window with one arm over the passenger seat, steers toward the intended rear path, and never backs on a freeway or interstate.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: For how many seconds must you signal before turning or changing lanes, and what curb moves also require signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Signals by lamp or hand and arm are required for two seconds before turning, for two seconds before any lane change, and whenever pulling to or from a curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What four-step sequence completes a safe lane change in Utah?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: A lane change requires mirror checks, a signal held for at least two seconds, an over-shoulder blind-spot check, and a safe merge before cancelling.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: How must you manage lane lines during ordinary travel, turns, and crossing intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: A driver stays inside marked lanes, finishes a turn in the lane corresponding to the entry lane, and avoids lane changes inside intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Who holds right-of-way at a highway merge, and what painted triangle is off-limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: A merging driver yields to traffic already in the continuing lane and never drives across or inside the solid-white gore area.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: How does the zipper method work when heavy traffic approaches a lane-ending merge point?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: At a congested merge point drivers use the zipper method by filling both lanes to the merge point and then alternating entry into the single lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How much clearance from oncoming traffic must remain when returning right after a pass, and what right-pass rule applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: A passing driver enters the left lane after checks and signal, returns no less than two hundred feet from oncoming traffic, and never leaves the roadway to pass on the right.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Alongside hills, curves, intersections, rails, and bridges, what snowplow situations ban passing in Utah?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Passing is prohibited with oncoming traffic, blocked view on a curve or hill, at intersections and stopped crosswalks, before rail crossings and bridges, in no-passing zones, and beside a deployed snowplow blade or echelon formation.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What sight-distance rule and three roadway locations prohibit making a U-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: A driver never makes a U-turn where visibility is blocked within five hundred feet in both directions, where a device prohibits it, on rail tracks or crossings, or on a freeway.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R05.front: At least how many feet clear of approaching oncoming traffic must you finish returning to the right lane?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R05.expected_back: A driver returning after a pass must be at least two hundred feet clear of approaching traffic before moving back right.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R06.front: What two passing bans apply around snowplows operating with flashing yellow lights?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R06.expected_back: A motorist near a snowplow showing flashing yellow lamps must not pass on the side where the blade is out, and must not pass at all when three or more plows run in echelon.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R09.front: How does a forward two-point turn differ from a reverse two-point turn using a driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R09.expected_back: A forward two-point turn enters a driveway or alley first and then backs out, while a reverse two-point turn drives past the driveway and then backs into it.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R10.front: Where is a three-point turn appropriate, and where are U-turns strictly barred?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R10.expected_back: A three-point turn belongs only on a narrow two-lane road, and a U-turn is barred where sight distance falls short of five hundred feet both ways, on curves and hilltops, tracks, crossings, freeways, and posted no-U-turn spots.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R11.front: In what exact order do mirrors, two-second signal, shoulder check, and signal cancel happen on a lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R11.expected_back: A lane change calls for mirrors first, a signal held at least two seconds, an over-shoulder blind-spot look, and a signal cancel after merging.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R12.front: How do normal merge yielding, solid-white gore lines, and jammed zipper merges fit together?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R12.expected_back: A merging driver must yield to nearby through-lane traffic and must not enter the solid-white gore zone, while at a jammed merge point drivers use the full lanes and take turns under the zipper method.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Where do you halt at a stop sign or light, and what visual cue sets safe spacing behind a stopped car?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: At a stop sign or signal the driver stops before the stop line, crosswalk, sidewalk, or intersection, and behind another vehicle leaves room to see its rear wheels.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What complete sequence secures a vehicle parked facing downhill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: For downhill parking the driver signals right, pulls parallel to the curb, turns the front wheels toward the curb so a tire contacts it, then sets park and the parking brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Which way do front wheels point when parking uphill with a curb versus uphill with no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: For uphill parking with a curb the driver turns the front wheels away from the curb with tire contact, and without a curb turns them to the right, then sets park and the brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Within how many inches of the curb must a parked vehicle sit, and what three shutdown steps apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: A parked vehicle beside a curb sits no more than twelve inches from the curb, with the motor stopped, brake set, and doors locked.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: Within what distance window from the nearest rail must you stop at an active or stop-controlled railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: At a rail crossing controlled by signals, gates, a watchman, or a stop sign the driver stops more than fifteen feet but not more than fifty feet from the nearest rail and waits for a raised gate.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: On which two roadway layouts do both directions stop for red school-bus lights, and on which two do opposing lanes continue?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.memory_hook: Undivided two-four stop, median five-turn go
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Traffic both directions stops for flashing red school-bus lights on a two-lane road and on a four-lane road without a median, while only the lanes behind the bus stop on a median-divided highway with four or more lanes and on a highway with five or more lanes plus a shared center turn lane.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R01.front: Beside a raised curb, how do downhill versus uphill front-wheel angles oppose each other?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R01.expected_back: A downhill-parked car has its front wheels rolled toward the curb so the curb blocks rolling, while an uphill-parked car with a curb has them rolled away from the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R02.front: Which way must you steer your front tires when parking uphill along a road shoulder without a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R02.expected_back: Uphill parking where no curb exists calls for steering the front wheels toward the road edge instead of away from it.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R03.front: How close to the curb must your rear tire and finished parallel-parking position rest?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R03.expected_back: A car parked beside a curb must keep its back wheel within a foot of the curb, and a parallel-parked car must finish within a foot of the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R04.front: What no-parking distances apply in Utah near fire hydrants, crosswalks, signs or signals, and railroad rails?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R04.expected_back: Utah bars parking within fifteen feet of a hydrant, within twenty feet of a crosswalk, within thirty feet of a beacon or sign or signal, and within fifty feet of the closest rail of a crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R07.front: How do median dividers or a five-lane shared center turn lane change oncoming school-bus stopping duties?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R07.expected_back: Traffic in both directions must halt for a bus flashing red lamps on a two-lane road or a four-lane road without a median, while only the same-direction lanes must halt on a divided highway or a five-lane road with a shared center turn lane.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R08.front: Between what minimum and maximum distances from the nearest rail must you stop at a controlled crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R08.expected_back: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, gates, a watchman, or a stop sign, the driver must halt farther than fifteen feet but no farther than fifty feet from the nearest rail.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What immediate action is legally required of every driver involved in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: A driver in a crash must stop at once and stay at the scene

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: How long can Utah suspend or revoke your license for leaving a crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Leaving the scene can bring license suspension or revocation for up to one year

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What maximum jail term and dollar fine can follow leaving a Utah crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Leaving the scene can also bring jail for up to one year or a fine of up to two thousand five hundred dollars

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What two duties do involved drivers owe anyone injured in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: An involved driver must give reasonable aid and arrange transport for the hurt when needed

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Which three crash outcomes require calling law enforcement immediately in Utah?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: A driver must call law enforcement at once when there is injury, death, or at least two thousand five hundred dollars in damage

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Which four pieces of driver, vehicle, and policy information must crash participants exchange?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Drivers must swap name, address, registration number, and insurance contact details

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How long must an involved driver remain after halting at a crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: An involved driver must halt at once at the scene and stay until duties are done, with leaving carrying severe penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: When only property is damaged, may you move your car out of traffic before exchanging details?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: A driver in a property-damage-only crash may clear travel lanes to a safe nearby spot, but must remain until exchange duties finish.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: What three crash triggers require immediate law-enforcement notification rather than private exchange alone?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Notice to law enforcement is required at once when a crash brings injury, death, or the stated total property-damage threshold.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: During what afternoon hours do most crashes cluster, and what share involves driver error?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Most crashes cluster between two pm and six pm, and driver error factors into seventy-five percent of crashes

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: How should you apply the parking brake if regular brakes fail, and why stay ready?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: With dead brakes, ease on the parking brake slowly and be ready to release it in a skid

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How do you brake hard with antilock brakes when the pedal vibrates and clicks?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: With ABS, push the pedal down hard and hold it while vibration and clicking remain normal

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Which four visibility steps protect a disabled car, including exact flare distance behind it?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: A disabled vehicle needs flashers, a raised hood, a bright marker, and flares set two hundred to three hundred feet back

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Along with flashers, raised hood, marker cloth, and rear warning devices, what completes breakdown safety?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: A disabled vehicle must be made visible with flashers, hood signal, marker cloth, warning devices placed well behind, plus a call for help.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: How does emergency braking and steering with antilock brakes differ from a non-equipped vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes keep the pedal pressed hard through vibration and keep steering, while a non-equipped car follows its manual method.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What criminal misdemeanor class and credential losses hit a driver operating without required security?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Driving without required security is a class B misdemeanor tied to license and registration loss

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: After how many days does an unpaid crash judgment suspend driving privileges, and what restores them?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: An unpaid crash judgment suspends driving privilege after sixty days until paid with SR22 future proof

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: How many years must required future financial-responsibility proof normally remain on file?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Required future proof is normally kept for three years after suspension, revocation, or reinstatement

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Which two Utah coverages are mandatory by law, and who typically requires collision and comprehensive?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Liability and PIP or no-fault coverages are mandatory while collision and comprehensive are lien-holder driven

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Beyond a misdemeanor charge, which three items can operating without owner security cost until settled?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Operating without required owner security is a misdemeanor class that can cost license, registration, and plates until proof and payments return.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What two steps lift a license suspension caused by an unsatisfied crash-damage judgment?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: An unsatisfied damage judgment suspends driving privilege after the stated grace period until paid plus future-proof filing.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do Utah's two legally required coverages separate from uninsured-motorist, collision, and comprehensive policies?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Required liability and no-fault injury benefits differ from uninsured-motorist injury cover, collision cover, and comprehensive non-collision cover.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which three Utah credentials allow a state resident to drive legally on a public roadway?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Every Utah resident operating a motor vehicle on a public roadway must hold a valid Utah license, learner permit, or temporary license.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which five actions classify someone as a Utah resident for driver-licensing purposes?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Utah treats a person as a resident after entering to make Utah home, staying six months in a calendar year, licensing or registering in Utah, taking resident-only privileges like tuition, or taking Utah employment except temporary assignment.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Does spending six months in Utah within a single calendar year establish licensing residency by itself?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A six-month presence in Utah during any calendar year alone makes a person a resident for licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Which two everyday living milestones immediately make someone a Utah resident for licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back:
grp: residency; pre: none; dif: one; conf: sec02-R03
Utah home or six months stay makes resident

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What must every Utah resident carry to operate a motor vehicle on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back:
grp: need; pre: sec02-R01; dif: two; conf: sec02-R04
Resident needs valid license or permit on roads

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: At what minimum age may a nonresident drive in Utah using a valid home-state or foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A nonresident at least age sixteen holding a valid license from another state or country may drive in Utah.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which temporarily assigned workers and military households may keep driving on valid out-of-state or foreign licenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Nonresidents on temporary assignment for an employer, religious or private organization, or government entity, and nonresident military personnel and dependents on temporary Utah assignment, may drive on a valid out-of-state or out-of-country license.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which age, record, exam, warrant, residency, or teen-training gaps block someone from getting a Utah license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A person may not hold a Utah license if under age sixteen, if driving privilege is denied, suspended, revoked, or disqualified here or elsewhere, if unable to drive safely, if required exams are not passed, if an unsettled citation or warrant remains, if not a state resident, or if under eighteen without six months on a learner permit plus driver education.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which three types of construction or farm machines need no driver license on Utah highways during work?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Road rollers, road machinery, and farm tractors on Utah highways need no driver license when used in construction or agricultural work.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Up to how long may a visitor drive in Utah on a valid out-of-state or foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A visitor with a valid out-of-state or out-of-country license may drive in Utah for up to six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: How many federally compliant star-marked credentials may one person hold across states at the same time?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A person may hold only one REAL ID-compliant credential at a time, so a Utah license and another state's ID cannot both be REAL ID.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: What minimum age and maximum stay govern a licensed visitor driving in Utah?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back:
grp: visitor; pre: sec02-R01; dif: two; conf: sec02-R01
Licensed visitor age sixteen plus may drive six months

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Which basic age cutoff and privilege status immediately disqualify a Utah license applicant?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back:
grp: bars; pre: sec02-R01; dif: two; conf: sec02-R02
Under sixteen or denied privilege bars license

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which two interstate compacts include Utah, and what does the forty-five-state plus District of Columbia compact share?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Utah belongs to the Driver License Compact and Non-Resident Violator Compact; the DLC shares driver records and convictions with the home state, with forty-five states plus the District of Columbia as members.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which states stay outside each interstate compact, and what happens when an out-of-state citation goes unanswered?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: DLC nonmembers are Georgia, Massachusetts, Wisconsin, Michigan, and Tennessee; NRVC has forty-four states plus the District of Columbia, with Alaska, California, Michigan, Montana, Oregon, and Wisconsin outside it, and the home state suspends until citation terms are met.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: What information does the Driver License Compact share, and how many states remain outside it?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back:
grp: DLC; pre: sec02-R02; dif: three; conf: sec02-R06
DLC shares records; nonmembers are five states

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: What does the Non-Resident Violator Compact forward, and how many states remain outside it?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back:
grp: NRVC; pre: sec02-R05; dif: three; conf: sec02-R05
NRVC forwards citations; nonmembers are six states

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What minimum age and personal-vehicle weight ceiling apply to a regular Utah Class D license?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: A regular Class D credential at age sixteen or older covers personal vehicles up to twenty-six thousand pounds.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What prerequisite applies under age nineteen, and how are Class D holders under twenty-one classified?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Applicants younger than nineteen need approved driver education or an out-of-state or out-of-country license, and drivers under twenty-one receive a provisional Class D under a separate point system.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: How do Utah Classes A, B, C, and D separate vehicles by weight, towed units, cargo, and minimum age?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Class A and Class B concern combined or single vehicles over twenty-six thousand one pounds with a towed unit over ten thousand one pounds and intrastate limits at ages eighteen to twenty, Class C covers smaller buses and hazmat at minimum age twenty-one, and Class D covers other non-motorcycle vehicles at minimum age sixteen.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Which two core limits define the Utah Class D scope grouping?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Class D scope groups with age and weight limits.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: What primary measurement groups commercial Classes A, B, and C together?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Class A, B or C scope groups with combined-weight limits.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Which three specialized hauling or transport uses are grouped under endorsement codes?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Endorsement codes group hazmat, tanker and passenger uses.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Which three operating areas do Utah license restriction codes narrow down?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Restriction codes limit vehicle, speed and medical conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How does eligibility differ between a Utah limited-term credential and a driving privilege card?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: A limited-term credential goes to a non-citizen with verified lawful status that qualifies for REAL ID, while a driving privilege card covers a parolee or other lawfully present person ineligible for REAL ID and an undocumented immigrant.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Which identity documents qualify for a regular Class D or identification card, and which birth records get rejected?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: A regular Class D or ID identity showing needs one of a valid unexpired passport or card, a state-certified birth certificate, a consular birth-abroad report, a permanent resident card, or a naturalization or citizenship certificate, with hospital, miniature, laminated, or photocopied birth records rejected.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which documents satisfy Utah's Social Security requirement if you lack a signed government card?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Social security showing needs a signed government card or else a W-two, SSA-one thousand ninety-nine, non-SSA-one thousand ninety-nine, pay stub, or an agency ineligibility letter tied to lawful presence status.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How many Utah address documents are needed, how recent must they be, and which records qualify?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Utah residence and mailing showing needs two documents bearing name and address and dated within ninety days, drawn from bank statement, court papers, mortgage or rental contract, major credit-card bill, property-tax notice, school transcript, utility bill, or vehicle title.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Which three proof categories combine to form Utah's core licensing document triad?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Identity, residence and driving-experience proofs form the triad.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What proves driving experience for a first Utah license, and which two credentials skip it?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: First Utah license proof of driving experience means driver-education completion when under nineteen, or else an existing driving privilege from another state or country, and it is not required for a learner permit or ID card.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which two unexpired, electronically verified document options establish limited-term identity and lawful status?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: For limited-term identity and lawful-status proof, supply one unexpired document: either a DHS employment authorization document, verified through SAVE, or a foreign passport with a valid visa and I-ninety-four, also verified through SAVE.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: What rules govern photocopies and name mismatches at the licensing counter, and what does a bounced check cost?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Office-visit papers must be originals or agency-certified copies with faxed or photocopied papers refused, any name difference needs a legal name-change paper, and a returned check costs a twenty-dollar service charge to keep the privilege.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Which layered identity records, tax proof, and fingerprint item are required for an original driving privilege card?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: A driving privilege card needs one primary paper such as a foreign birth certificate or unexpired foreign passport with translation when needed, plus one secondary paper such as church, court, school, employee, insurance, consular, voter, license, or prior DPC records, plus SSN or ITIN proof and a sealed fingerprint card with photo for an original.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Can a driving privilege card verify age or identity, when does it expire, and can you drive before mail delivery?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: A driving privilege card is for driving only and is not valid identification or age verification, it expires each year on the holder birthday, and no temporary card or drive time is allowed before the plastic card arrives by mail.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: When do original adult over-twenty-one licenses expire compared with under-twenty-one provisional licenses?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: An original license generally expires on the holder birthday eight years after issue when over twenty-one, while a provisional license issued under age twenty-one expires on the holder birthday five years after issue.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How does Utah treat six-month visitor licenses, out-of-state learner permits, and old licenses upon Utah application?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: A visitor with a valid out-of-state or out-of-country license may drive in Utah for up to six months, an out-of-state learner permit does not allow driving in Utah, and an out-of-state license must be surrendered when applying for Utah.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: How early may you renew, what qualifies for online good-driver renewal, and how fast must Class D moves report?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Renewal may be sought up to six months before expiration with a new eight-year license from the birthday after issue, the good-driver online extension needs no more than six reportable violations in eight years with valid status, and change of address needs notice within ten days for Class D.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: What shared element links Utah renewal, replacement, and address-change responsibilities together?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Renewal, replacement and address-change duties group by timing.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Who is eligible for a Utah identification card, and may someone hold both a Utah license and identification card?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Only a Utah resident may hold an ID card, and Utah law forbids holding a license certificate and an ID card at the same time.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Where does Utah's written knowledge test pull its material from, and what does it verify?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: The written knowledge test samples handbook material to confirm basic grasp of Utah law and safe driving habits.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Is Utah's written knowledge test timed, how long does it usually take, and what score passes?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: The knowledge test is untimed and typically takes thirty to forty-five minutes, with passing set at eighty percent or better.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: How many written knowledge tests may a candidate take in one day, and what follows a failed try?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: A candidate may take two knowledge tests in one day when the Division can accommodate them, and a failed attempt needs a scheduled retest visit.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: How many written-test attempts and months does a single application fee cover?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: One fee covers up to three knowledge-test attempts within twelve months, and after three failures another fee buys three more attempts.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Which two administrative boundaries pair together to govern written-test retakes in the Utah manual?

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What additional online exam must first-time Class D applicants pass, and what score is required?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: First-time Class D applicants must also pass a Traffic Safety and Trends exam with a one hundred percent score, taken online as often as needed before licensing.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What topic accounts for half the questions on Utah's Traffic Safety and Trends exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Half the Safety and Trends questions cover major causes of traffic death drawn from Utah Highway Safety Office statistics.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How does the minimum age to take the driving-skills exam differ between the DLD and a high school or Third-Party Tester?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: The minimum skills-test age is sixteen years at the DLD and fifteen years with a Third-Party Tester or high school.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What basic vehicle condition and cabin-occupant rule apply during the driving-skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: The skills test requires a properly registered, safe vehicle with working belts, and only applicant plus examiner may ride along.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Which registration, lighting, glass, mirror, door, seat, and brake items are checked before your road test starts?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: The test vehicle needs current rear-plate registration, front and rear signals plus brake lights, horn, sound tires, firm brakes, opening driver window, clear windshield, two mirrors with a left-outside mirror, doors opening inside and out, fixed passenger seat, belts, and parking brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What broad range of habits and maneuvers do examiners grade during Utah's driving-skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Scored skills include attitude, technique, posture and lane use, turns, starts and stops, hill and parallel parking, signs and signals, backing, U-turns, steering, intersections, lane changes, and safe operation.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Which two road-exam topics does the handbook group together when summarizing behind-the-wheel testing?

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What practice, daily limit, three-strike fee, and overall completion deadline govern driving-skills tests?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: A failed skills test needs more practice first, allows only one skills test per day with possible waits, needs another fee after three failures, and all tests must finish within six months of paying.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which seven dangerous or unlawful mistakes trigger automatic failure on the Utah skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Automatic skills-test failure follows a moving citation or ignored law, missed yield, avoidable contact, forcing evasive action, needless curb or sidewalk contact, examiner takeover, or driving much too fast or too slow.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How does alcohol impair your ability to handle unfamiliar traffic situations?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Alcohol weakens judgment that draws on stored experience for new problems.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which sense is most vital for driving, and at what blood alcohol mark is it harmed?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Vision is the main driving sense and is harmed at zero point zero two BAC for each driver.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to begin impairing motor-vehicle operation?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: A single alcoholic drink can already impair the ability to drive a motor vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: When does alcohol harm begin, and what is the safest driving decision after drinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Harm starts with the first drink, so the safest choice is not to drive after use.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Beyond alcohol, which three drug sources and mental state can impair safe driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Illegal, store-bought, and prescribed drugs plus strong emotions can impair driving.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Which four driving skills drop from the first drink, making feeling drunk a bad test?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Impairment of driving judgment, vision, color perception, and reaction speed begins with the first drink, so waiting to feel visibly drunk is not a safe standard.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Why can someone lose sharp eyesight and vehicle control well before appearing intoxicated?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Vision used for driving is affected at a very low alcohol level, while a single drink can already degrade vehicle control even before obvious intoxication appears.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Which three practical steps protect safety when anger, worry, excitement, fear, or sadness strike?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Strong feelings such as anger, worry, excitement, fear, or sadness can distract thinking and degrade driving, and should be resolved by cooling off, allowing extra trip time, or letting another person drive.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Which three alcohol actions are completely unlawful for anyone under age twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Under age twenty-one it is unlawful to buy, hold, or drink alcohol under zero tolerance.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: How long do drivers aged thirteen through twenty lose licenses for first and repeat alcohol acts?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Ages thirteen through twenty face license loss of one year then two years for alcohol acts.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What privilege loss hits an under-twenty-one driver with measurable alcohol on first versus ten-year repeat offenses?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one who has measurable alcohol in the body faces denial of driving privileges for six months on the first offense. A repeat offense within ten years of an earlier denial brings a loss lasting two years or through the twenty-first birthday, with the longer period controlling.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What blood alcohol mark breaks Utah's general driving law versus its commercial-driver threshold?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Over zero point zero five BAC breaks the law, and zero point zero four does so for CDL holders in Utah.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Can an adult twenty-one or older break Utah's alcohol driving law while testing below the general number?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: A driver age twenty-one or older violates the alcohol law above the stated general operating threshold, with a lower threshold for commercial operation, and can also violate by being unsafe below those numbers.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: What court penalty hits youths thirteen through twenty for alcohol possession, drinking, or underage bar entry?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: A person aged thirteen through twenty convicted of possessing alcohol, consuming alcohol, or entering a bar while underage faces a court-ordered license suspension that lengthens on a repeat offense, with timing anchored to conviction or to the sixteenth birthday for the youngest drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Does Utah's under-twenty-one measurable-alcohol denial still apply if the young driver holds no license yet?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one with any measurable alcohol in the body faces denial of driving privileges for months on a first occurrence and for years or until age twenty-one on a repeat within a decade, even if no license has yet been issued.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How do first and repeat adult DUI suspension lengths compare, and when does administrative suspension start?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A first driving-under-influence conviction at twenty-one or older suspends the license for months, while a second or later conviction suspends it for years, with administrative suspension authority beginning weeks after arrest.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: How long is your license revoked for refusing an officer's chemical test as an adult versus under twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Refusal of the chemical test selected by the officer brings license revocation: eighteen months for a first offense, then thirty-six months for repeat offenses. For someone younger than twenty-one, the first revocation lasts two years or through the twenty-first birthday, whichever lasts longer. A repeat revocation for that younger driver lasts thirty-six months or through that birthday, again using the longer period.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: How long does a first DUI require an in-car breath device for adults versus arrests under twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A first DUI brings an eighteen-month car device term, or three years if under twenty-one at arrest.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What credential step and administrative fee apply when a court designates someone an interdicted person?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A court-called interdicted person gives up the card and pays a seven point zero zero admin fee.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Which four chemical sample types do Utah road and motorboat operators agree to under implied consent?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Driving or operating a motorboat implies agreement to breath, blood, urine, or oral-fluid testing when a peace officer requests it, and refusing causes a longer revocation that grows on repeat offenses, with a special until-age-twenty-one rule for younger drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How long can alcohol-restricted status last, and what happens if caught driving with any alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: After an alcohol-related action, a driver carries an alcohol-restricted status for a multi-year tier or for life depending on offense count and type, and driving with any measurable alcohol during that period revokes the license for a year.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: How does interlock duration scale from an adult first DUI to underage, repeat, or test-refusal cases?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: A first driving-under-influence conviction brings an ignition-interlock-only driving period measured in months, longer when the driver was under twenty-one at arrest, while a second or later covered violation or a test-refusal revocation brings a multi-year interlock period.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: How often must an ignition interlock undergo service checks, and what adds extra time?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: An interlock-restricted driver must have the device checked at least about every two months, and each missed check or attempt to start with measurable alcohol adds about two more months to the requirement.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: How does voluntary alcohol-interdicted status differ from court-ordered interdiction in fees and minimum duration?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A court-designated interdicted person surrenders the license or card and pays a small administrative fee to add interdicted status, while a voluntary applicant completes an agreement form without that fee and must keep the status for at least about a month.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: What happens if you knowingly present a canceled, suspended, or altered license, or tamper with one?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Showing a license you know is canceled, suspended, or altered is unlawful, and altering a license can bring suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What file does the division maintain on every Utah driver, and how long do ordinary moving convictions post?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: The division keeps a computerized driving and crash history for every state driver, posting moving-violation convictions and suspensions from the prior three years.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How long do alcohol-linked or drug-linked violations, suspensions, and revocations remain on your Utah driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Alcohol and drug linked violations, suspensions, and revocations stay on the driving record for ten years.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Which two national databases receive commercial driver records, suspensions, and revocations?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: A commercial driver record goes to the commercial license information system, with suspensions and revocations sent on to the national driver registry.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What jail term and financial penalty can follow driving while your privilege is denied, suspended, or revoked?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Operating while denied, suspended, or revoked can draw jail of ninety days plus a fine.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How does getting caught driving while denied, suspended, or revoked extend your original time off the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: The original denial, suspension, or revocation period grows by that same original length, so a three-month suspension gains another three months.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Which dishonest actions involving a driver license card can trigger suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Showing a canceled, suspended, or altered license, or altering a license, can bring suspension

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does Utah's record retention time for routine moving convictions compare against alcohol and drug actions?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Routine moving convictions stay on the record for three years, while alcohol and drug actions stay for ten years

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: What higher fine and custody ceilings apply if you drive while suspended or revoked on an alcohol-related basis?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: When the underlying suspension or revocation is alcohol related, the fine can reach one thousand dollars and custody can reach six months.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Up to how long, or until what birthday, can a mandatory-grounds Utah suspension run?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: A suspension for mandatory grounds can run as long as two years or until age twenty-one.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which driving offenses, point totals, substance findings, and court failures can suspend a Utah license?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Suspension grounds include a mandatory-suspension conviction, a crash from reckless or unlawful conduct with injury, death, or serious property harm, license misuse, point-system buildup, DUI or drug findings, and court nonappearance or unpaid obligations.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Which insurance, family-law, texting, underage-alcohol, course, and first road-rage violations also bring suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Further suspension grounds include missing no-fault insurance or financial responsibility, unpaid child support, a court-ordered texting suspension, underage alcohol proof misuse, custodial interference, an uncompleted emergency-vehicle course, and a first road-rage citation carrying a one-year court suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Which high-severity crimes, repeat substance findings, test refusals, and repeat road-rage cases trigger full revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Revocation follows findings such as manslaughter or auto homicide, a repeat intoxicated-control offense, a false oath on application, felony use of a vehicle, failing to aid after a fatal or injury crash, fleeing police, firing or releasing weapons or incendiary items from a vehicle, restricted-status alcohol or interlock breaches, ordered careless-driving revocation, auto homicide with a handheld device, test refusal, and two road-rage citations in a year.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: How many points attach to reckless driving, speeding, yield or tailgating, red lights or texting, and minor moving violations?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Point values assign eighty to reckless driving, thirty-five to seventy-five for speeding by severity, sixty to yield, tailgating, wrong side, and wrong way, fifty to red light, stop sign, lookout, passing, and texting, and forty to other moving violations.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: How do clean conviction-free years and a division-recommended defensive course trim points off your Utah record?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Half the points leave after one conviction-free year, all points leave after two straight conviction-free years, each conviction drops at three years, and a division-recommended defensive course erases fifty points once in any three-year span.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: Which two specific handbook examples illustrate findings that bring revocation rather than suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Suspension and revocation differ, with repeat intoxicated control and false sworn statements leading to revocation

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: At what three-year point totals do older drivers versus younger drivers trigger a division hearing?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: A hearing is triggered at two hundred points in three years for older drivers and seventy points for younger drivers

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Summarize how one clean year, two clean years, and one defensive course reduce Utah record points?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Half the points clear after one clean year, all clear after two clean years, and one course removes fifty points

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Which ten roadside and roadway travelers does Utah law group together as vulnerable highway users?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Utah treats pedestrians, highway workers, animal riders, farm gear without a cab, boards, skates, cycles, scooters, motorcycles and wheelchairs as vulnerable highway users.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: What consequence can follow intentionally distracting a vulnerable road user to threaten harm or crowd them off the pavement?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Deliberately distracting a vulnerable road user in order to threaten harm or push that person off the road can lead to a citation with points on the driving record.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What three consequences follow intentionally distracting or pushing an unprotected traveler off the street?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Deliberately distracting or forcing a vulnerable user off the road can bring a citation, record entry and points.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: What legal status, rights, and responsibilities apply to bicycles ridden on Utah roads?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Bicycles on the road count as vehicles with the same rights and duties as cars.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Where must drivers yield to bicycles, and what are the three sole reasons a car may enter a marked bike lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Drivers yield to bikes at crossings and keep off marked bike lanes except to enter a drive, obey police or handle an emergency.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: At least how many feet of side clearance does Utah require when overtaking a cyclist or any vulnerable user?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: When passing any bicyclist or vulnerable user, Utah requires at least three feet of clearance.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How much lateral space must a motorist leave beside a bicycle rider while passing?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: A driver passing a person on a bicycle must leave at least three feet of space beside that rider.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: How far away must you dim brights for cyclists at night, and what parked checks protect riders?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Drivers dim headlights within five hundred feet when near bikes at night and check before opening doors or backing.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: At which six sight-limited features—or within one hundred feet of them—is passing a bicycle or moped forbidden?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: A bike or moped may be passed only where sight lines allow, never blindly over a crest, curve, bridge, tunnel, crossing or within one hundred feet of them.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Within how many feet from ten miles per hour must a bicycle brake stop, and what night visibility is required?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: A bike brake must halt the machine within twenty-five feet from ten miles per hour, and night riders need white front, red rear and side visibility.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Which front, rear, and side lighting or reflector colors must a bicycle display whenever lights are needed?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: A bicycle ridden when lights are needed must show a white front light plus red rear and side reflectors that remain visible from far down the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What immediate action is mandatory when an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens or flashing lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: On sirens or flashing emergency signals, drivers must pull at once to the right edge and halt until the vehicle passes.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How must a driver respond upon meeting an emergency vehicle running sirens or flashing warning lamps?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: A driver meeting an emergency vehicle using sirens or flashing warning lights must promptly move to the right edge and halt until it goes by.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: What three steps apply when approaching a vehicle stopped at the roadside with flashing hazards or amber lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Near a stopped roadside vehicle with hazards or amber lamps, slow down, give space and move a lane away when safe.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How must you adjust speed and lane choice when coming upon a stopped roadside car flashing its hazard lights?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: A driver coming upon a stopped roadside vehicle with flashing hazard lights must slow down, give generous room, and shift one lane away when it can be done safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What classroom requirement or suspension consequence follows a conviction for violating Utah's move-over law?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Ignoring the move-over rule and being convicted means a four-hour classroom course within ninety days or a ninety-day suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: What is the standard maximum vehicle width in Utah, and what wider limit applies to farm tractors?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: No vehicle may exceed eight and one-half feet in width, while farm tractors may reach nine feet.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What maximum height, single-unit length, and general combination length apply to Utah road vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Road vehicles are capped at fourteen feet high, forty-five feet for a single unit, and sixty-five feet for most other combinations.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: How far may cargo extend past the front, rear, left side, and right side of a vehicle body?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Loads may project at most three feet ahead and six feet behind the body, with side overhang barred on the left and capped at six inches on the right.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Why do tractor-trailers often run the center lane, and what two misjudgments trap passenger-car drivers around them?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Tractor-trailers favor the center lane on multilane roads, need far longer braking room and mislead judges of speed at crossings.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, how does a passenger car's stopping distance compare with a loaded tractor-trailer?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: A car at fifty-five miles per hour stops in about one hundred thirty to one hundred forty feet, while a loaded rig can need over four hundred feet.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Why do long rigs swing left before turning right, and what must trailing drivers avoid doing?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Long rigs swing left first for a right turn, so followers must wait for the maneuver to finish rather than squeeze past.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: How far ahead, beside, and behind a large truck do its blind areas extend?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Truck blind areas reach about twenty feet ahead, along both flanks by the cab, and up to two hundred feet behind.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Where do large trucks hide nearby cars, and how does the truck's side mirror reveal whether you are visible?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: A large truck hides vehicles directly ahead of its cab, along both sides near the cab, and far behind its trailer, so a car unseen in the truck mirror is unseen by the trucker.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: What simple visual test tells you instantly whether a semi-truck driver can see your car?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: If a driver cannot see the trucker in the side mirror, the trucker cannot see that driver.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: After overtaking a large truck, what must appear in your inside rearview mirror before pulling back right?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Before returning after passing a large rig, the passer must see its full front in the rear-view mirror.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Why must you never dart tight in front of a fast-moving loaded truck?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: A driver should never pull directly ahead of a fast-moving heavy truck because the loaded truck needs a much longer distance to halt than a car does.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What registration and licensing exemption applies to qualifying mobility-permit and pedestrian vehicles on Utah highways?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Mobility permits and pedestrian vehicles can use highways under stated conditions without standard registration or licensing.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What supervision rule governs scooter riders under fifteen, and which roadways stay off-limits?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Riders under fifteen need supervision or a certificate for motor-assisted scooters, and such scooters stay off fast or wide roads and posted no-board areas.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Under what exact road-type, speed-limit, stopped-traffic, and rider-speed conditions may a motorcycle lane-filter?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Lane filtering past stopped traffic is allowed only on same-direction multilane roads or off-ramps capped at forty-five miles per hour, at fifteen miles per hour or less and only when safe.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: How does Utah's lawful motorcycle lane filtering differ from unlawful lane splitting?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Slow filtering past stopped cars on a motorcycle is allowed only on suitable multilane roads at very low speed, while weaving between moving cars remains unlawful.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Why must you confirm a motorcycle is genuinely slowing to turn rather than trusting its flashing turn signal?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: A motorcycle's flashing turn signal does not prove the rider will turn. Many motorcycle signals require manual cancellation, and the rider might have left one operating accidentally.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: How much of the street must a crossing pedestrian clear before a stopped driver may roll forward?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Drivers stay halted until a walker clears at least their half of the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: Once halted for a pedestrian, when is your vehicle allowed to proceed?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: A vehicle halted for a pedestrian must stay stopped until the walker has cleared at least the half of the roadway the driver occupies.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: How must drivers respond to a white cane or guide dog, and how should pedestrians walk without sidewalks?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Walkers with a guide dog or white cane get a full stop, and walkers without sidewalks use the left shoulder facing traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: Below what speed do slow vehicles wear an orange-red triangle, and how must you pass horses?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Slow vehicles show an orange-red triangle when below twenty-five miles per hour, and horses get quiet wide passes without horn or revving.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: Which roads, top speed, and higher-limit lane position govern street-legal ATVs and UTVs?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Street-legal ATVs and UTVs use single-lane-each-way roads, keep to fifty miles per hour or less and hug the far right with reflector when the limit is higher.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: What tire-size, tread-depth, lighting, mirror, horn, eye-protection, and gauge rules apply to street-legal all-terrain rigs?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Stock no larger than manufacturer size with at least two thirty-seconds inch tread, plus lamps, signals, mirrors, horn, windshield or eye cover, and speedometer belong on street-legal all-terrain machines.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: At what distance band do you stop for tracks, and what parking and passing bans apply at crossings?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: At crossings halt fifteen to fifty feet from the rail, never park within fifty feet, and never pass another same-direction car there.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Where before the nearest rail must a driver stop when directed, and how long must they remain halted?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: A driver told to stop for a rail crossing must halt within a short marked band before the nearest rail and must stay stopped while the red lights keep flashing.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: What do flashing rail lights or bells demand, and when are crossing gates off-limits to bypass?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Flashing rail lights or bells mean full stop until they end, and gates must never be bypassed while moving or closed.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: May a driver ever steer around, duck under, or push through moving or lowered rail gates?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: A driver must never steer around, beneath, or through rail gates while they are moving or lowered.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Who holds right-of-way at crossings, and how far can a fifty-five-mile-per-hour loaded freight train travel before halting?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Trains hold full priority over every road user, may come either way without schedule, and a loaded freight at fifty-five miles per hour can run over a mile to halt.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: If your car stalls on tracks with a train approaching, which direction do you run after getting everyone out?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: A stalled car on train tracks must be emptied at once, and anyone escaping an oncoming train should run angled toward the train so wreckage flies away from them.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: At Utah light-rail crossings, what clearance and gate rules apply, and what does a flashing train emblem mean?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Light-rail crossings need full track clearance, waiting until gates lift and reds quit, with a flashing train emblem as caution only rather than a stop order.

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F01.front: What is the longest drawbar or tow connection permitted between a towing vehicle and the vehicle behind it?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F01.expected_back: The drawbar or other link between towing and towed vehicles may not be longer than fifteen feet from one vehicle to the other

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F02.front: When towing with a chain, rope, or cable, what size red cloth or signal must hang on the line?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F02.expected_back: When the tow connection is a chain, rope, or cable, a red flag or other signal at least twelve inches square must be fixed to the connection

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F03.front: What sideways trailer motion makes operating a towed combination unlawful?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F03.expected_back: A driver must not operate a combination of vehicles when any towed trailer or vehicle whips or swerves dangerously or unreasonably from side to side

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F04.front: What vehicle width, length, and stopped duration trigger mandatory roadside warning devices?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F04.expected_back: Warning devices must be shown when a disabled or stopped vehicle at least eighty inches wide or thirty feet long stays on the road for more than ten minutes

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F05.front: In which four everyday stopping situations are portable roadside warning devices unnecessary?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F05.expected_back: Warning devices are not required when legally parked in an urban district, lawfully loading passengers, stopped to avoid a conflict, or obeying an officer or traffic control device

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F06.front: During a roadside breakdown emergency, where do you set the very first warning lamp, reflector, or flare?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F06.expected_back: In an emergency, first set a flare, lighted fuse, electric lantern, or emergency reflector beside the vehicle on the side facing nearest oncoming traffic

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F07.front: After placing the side marker, at what distances ahead and behind do the remaining warning devices go?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F07.expected_back: Next place flares, electric lights, or reflectors one hundred feet ahead and behind the vehicle, plus one device on the traffic side at least ten feet behind the vehicle

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F08.front: Which hazardous-cargo vehicles are forbidden from carrying open-flame flares or fuses?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F08.expected_back: A vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquids, or compressed gas must not carry flares or fuses aboard

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F09.front: On a one-way roadway, how far behind a stopped vehicle does the handbook recommend setting the rear warning banner?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F09.expected_back: On a street carrying traffic in one direction, the handbook recommends positioning the rear warning flag two hundred feet behind the stopped vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F10.front: When does bright ambient lighting excuse setting out portable roadside warning devices?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F10.expected_back: Warning devices may be omitted when enough light makes people and vehicles visible from one thousand feet away

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F11.front: If you break down within five hundred feet past a blind curve or hillcrest, how far back must that warning marker move?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F11.expected_back: When a breakdown happens within five hundred feet before a curve, hilltop, or other blocked view, the device on that side must be moved farther out to warn approaching drivers, staying between one hundred feet and five hundred feet from the vehicle

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F12.front: Where across the lane or shoulder width must each portable warning device sit?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F12.expected_back: Every warning device must sit in the middle of the occupied lane, or on the shoulder as close as possible to the roadway when the vehicle is fully off the road

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F13.front: What three safety precautions govern handling a burning highway flare or fuse?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F13.expected_back: Keep a burning fuse or flare away from the face and eyes, never fasten a flare or fuse to the vehicle, and keep burning devices away from spilled fuel

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F14.front: Which tire-pressure, brake-release, and heat-check habits prevent dangerous highway tire fires?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F14.expected_back: Prevent tire fires by checking tires and brakes for unusual heat, changing soft or flat tires, never driving far on a soft or flat tire or with a dragging brake, never ignoring a hot tire, always releasing the parking brake before moving, and watching for dragging brakes, oil on hot tires, or partly deflated dual tires

sec16-card-sec16-towing-F15.front: How should you position yourself with an extinguisher, and why must you never throw water on gasoline or oil fires?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-F15.expected_back: Fight other fires by aiming each extinguisher burst carefully, keeping the wind at the back, and never using water on gasoline or oil fires because water only spreads them

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R01.front: At most how many feet may separate a towing vehicle from the vehicle it pulls?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R01.expected_back: A tow link between vehicles may span at most fifteen feet from one vehicle to the other

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R02.front: What warning attachment is mandatory on a chain, rope, or cable tow link, and how big must a cloth be?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R02.expected_back: A tow connection made from chain, rope or cable needs an attached red flag or another signal. If a flag is used, its size must be at least twelve inches square.

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R03.front: When must you refuse to drive a vehicle combination pulling a trailer or towed car?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R03.expected_back: Do not operate connected vehicles if a trailer or any other vehicle being towed swings from side to side in a dangerous or unreasonable way.

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R04.front: Summarize when wide or long disabled rigs require roadside markers and which stops or lighting excuse them?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R04.expected_back: Warning devices are required after more than ten minutes stopped or disabled beside the road when the vehicle is at least eighty inches wide or thirty feet long. Exceptions cover lawful urban parking, lawful passenger pickup or drop-off, avoiding a traffic conflict, and following an officer or official traffic control. Devices are also unnecessary when sufficient light makes people or vehicles visible from one thousand feet.

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R05.front: At least how far behind a stopped vehicle must the close traffic-side warning device sit?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R05.expected_back: Keep a traffic-side device at least ten feet behind the stopped vehicle

sec16-card-sec16-towing-R06.front: Is it ever acceptable to strap or attach a lit flare or burning fuse onto your vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-towing-R06.expected_back: Never fasten a lighted flare or fuse to the vehicle itself

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F01.front: Who carries direct responsibility for making sure a motorist is healthy enough to drive?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F01.expected_back: Each driver bears personal responsibility for being in reasonably good health while driving

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F02.front: What two steps must a driver take upon developing a medical condition that could impair safe driving?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F02.expected_back: A driver with a condition that may affect safe driving must report it and seek qualified health advice

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F03.front: Which three types of health care professionals can advise on a motorist's fitness to drive in Utah?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F03.expected_back: Health care professionals advising on driving fitness include doctors, physician assistants and advanced nurses

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F04.front: Which body maintains Utah's medical driving-fitness guidelines, and where can the public view them?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F04.expected_back: A medical advisory board maintains driving fitness guidelines available through the division website

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F05.front: How many medical categories do Utah's driving-fitness guidelines span, and what kinds of areas are included?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F05.expected_back: The guidelines cover eleven health groups from metabolic and heart conditions through vision, strength and sleep

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R01.front: How does Utah define a motorist's ongoing driver-fitness duty with health providers and the Division?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R01.expected_back: Driver fitness duty means the motorist stays healthy enough to drive and reports risky conditions to the Division after HCP review

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F06.front: What visual acuity and horizontal field-of-vision minimums apply for regular Class D driving in Utah?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F06.expected_back: Class D driving calls for at least twenty over forty vision in one eye plus at least ninety degrees of visual field

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F07.front: When does Utah require an applicant to complete a vision screening?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F07.expected_back: A vision check is required at the field office and for applicants older than sixty-five at application

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F08.front: What must an applicant do if they cannot pass the field-office vision screen?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F08.expected_back: Anyone unable to pass must carry an eye-exam certificate to an eye specialist and file acuity proof before approval

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F09.front: Which five emotional or behavioral warning signs show mental strain is hurting your driving?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F09.expected_back: Mental strain shows in anger at others, confusion in traffic, worry off the road, citations and grief reactions

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F10.front: How must you manage prescription or over-the-counter medicines that cause drowsiness?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F10.expected_back: Some medicines bring drowsiness, so dosing must be arranged with a doctor and misuse of prescriptions avoided
