sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R02.front: What complete eyesight standard and screening triggers govern regular Class D licensing in Utah?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R02.expected_back: For a regular Class D vehicle, vision must reach twenty over forty in at least one eye, with a field of vision measuring at least ninety degrees. A vision test is required when visiting a field office, or when applying for a license at an age older than sixty-five.

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R03.front: When do emotional strain and sedating medications warn you to stay out of the driver's seat?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R03.expected_back: Mind-state and medication caution says anger, confusion, distraction, citations and sedating doses warn against driving until calm and dosed safely

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F11.front: What happens after you answer the health screening questions on a Utah license application?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F11.expected_back: Applicants answer health questions, may receive a mailed ability form for their clinician, and face possible limits or retesting

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F12.front: Whose reports can prompt a Utah review exam, what happens if you ignore it, and how does the hearing officer decide?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-F12.expected_back: A review exam may follow medical, police or citizen reports, and skipping it ends driving; a hearing officer then weighs needs, roads and medical guidance

sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R04.front: After you complete a required Utah driver review, when are driving privileges actually withdrawn?
sec05-card-sec05-vision-health-R04.expected_back: After a completed driver review, the hearing officer considers the medical evaluation and the person's driving needs, roads and traffic, then decides on restrictions using Medical Advisory Board guidelines. When the review is completed, privileges are withdrawn only if the division finds safe driving impossible under any conditions. Failing to complete a required review also causes withdrawal.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What broad rule decides whether an activity counts as a driving distraction and crash hazard?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Anything drawing mind or body away from driving counts as a distraction and crash hazard.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: How long can your license be suspended on a first road-rage conviction tied to a roadway crime?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Utah road rage tied to a roadway criminal offense can bring a one-year license suspension on first conviction.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: How many nightly sleep hours do adults need to stay alert before starting a long drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep to stay alert, so do not start a long trip tired.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Where should you go and how long should you nap when fatigue strikes mid-drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: When fatigue hits, leave the road at an exit or rest area for a twenty-minute power nap.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: What extra element turns aggressive driving into legal road rage under Utah rules?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Aggressive operation that endangers others differs from road rage, which additionally requires a criminal act done from a vehicle to menace someone in another vehicle after a roadway incident

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Why does the Utah handbook instruct you to hold your lane rather than swerve for animals?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: If confused between staying in lane for an animal and swerving, the handbook rule is to keep control in the travel lane and not swerve, because swerving raises personal-injury risk

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Beyond emergency naps, which four habits belong in proactive fatigue-free trip planning?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.memory_hook: Night rest, two-hour breaks, companion, meds
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A mid-trip drowsy stop with a short nap differs from trip planning, which calls for nightly rest, a break about every two hours, a companion observer, and checking medicines for sleepiness

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: How little standing water stalls most cars, and what depth of moving water sweeps vehicles away?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Six inches of water can stall most cars, while two feet of moving water can carry away most vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Under what condition may a driver over eighteen talk on a phone while driving in Utah?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Drivers over eighteen may talk on a handheld device only with voice commands for hands-free calling.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: What misdemeanor class and fine cap hit a first texting offense, and what upgrades it to Class B?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: A texting conviction carries a Class C misdemeanor and a fine capped at one hundred dollars. Causing bodily injury or having an earlier violation of this offense raises it to a Class B misdemeanor.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What colors mark Utah work-zone signs, and how steep is the speeding fine inside one?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Work zone signs are orange with black letters, and speeding there draws at least twice the normal fine.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How do permitted phone uses compare between drivers eighteen-plus and drivers younger than eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Drivers at least eighteen may talk hands-free with voice commands plus GPS and hazard reporting, while drivers under eighteen may use a device only for medical, hazard, crime, or parent contact needs

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Which two circumstances elevate a Utah texting violation from the lower misdemeanor to the higher misdemeanor?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: A texting violation punished as the lower misdemeanor with a capped fine differs from the higher misdemeanor applied when bodily injury results or a prior offense exists

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Whether water merely reaches floor height or runs deeper across pavement, what action is required?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Shallow water reaching a car floor that causes loss of control differs from deeper moving water that can sweep away most vehicles including large trucks, and in both cases the rule is to turn around rather than cross

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How should you drive through an orange work zone when no crews appear, and when can you resume speed?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Orange work-zone signs with at least doubled speeding fines differ from ordinary signs, and drivers must slow even with no workers present, widen following space, and continue until the end-of-work notice

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Within how many feet must you dim high beams for oncoming traffic versus following behind a vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Dim high beams within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and within three hundred feet when following.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Below what sight distance must headlights come on, and where should your eyes look against oncoming glare?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Use lights whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead, and look to the right if blinded.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Above what speed can tires hydroplane on wet pavement, and how does black ice disguise itself?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Cars can hydroplane above thirty-five miles per hour, and black ice looks like a wet spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which way do you steer and how do you handle gas and brake pedals when the rear slides?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: If the rear slides right steer right, if it slides left steer left, ease off gas and avoid hard braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: How many seconds does a car typically float in water, and what two escape steps come first?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: A car entering water floats only thirty to sixty seconds, so remove the belt and open a window fast.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Between which exact calendar dates are studded snow tires legal on Utah roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Studded snow tires may be used from October fifteenth through March thirty-first each year.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: How many minutes per hour should you run the heater if snowbound, and what prevents carbon monoxide?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: If stranded in cold, run the engine about ten minutes each hour and keep one window cracked.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: After easing off the gas and steering gently into a rear skid, how do you finish recovery?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Steering toward the skid side differs from braking hard, so ease off the accelerator, steer gently the same way the rear slides, avoid oversteer and hard braking, then straighten once grip returns

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Who gets right-of-way on narrow mountain grades, how are gears used, and what warns blind curves?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Yielding to uphill traffic on a narrow descent differs from coasting in neutral, which is prohibited, and drivers should use a low gear, keep right, and sound the horn at blind sharp curves

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: How do escape priorities shift if a submerged car sinks before you can exit a window?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: A vehicle that floats only briefly after entering water calls for belt removal and window exit to the roof, while a fast-sinking vehicle with stuck exits calls for waiting for pressure balance, shedding heavy clothes, and using the air pocket

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Should you bleed air from hot tires, and what road-surface and headlight habits apply in heat or fog?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Letting hot-tire pressure stay high differs from bleeding it off, and drivers should also watch coolant gauges, expect slippery tar bleed, and use low beams in fog or snow

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: How do oncoming and following dim distances pair with night eyewear and poor-visibility spacing?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: Dimming for oncoming traffic at the longer distance differs from dimming when following at the shorter distance, and limited visibility also requires lights on and longer following space without tinted lenses at night

card-F01.front: Why must you check the overhead lane signal before pulling into a Utah flex lane?
card-F01.expected_back: Flex lanes may reverse direction by time of day; check the overhead signal before entering.

card-F02.front: What minimum following cushion applies on dry Utah freeways, and when must you stretch it?
card-F02.expected_back: Keep at least two seconds of following distance on the freeway; lengthen the gap when conditions worsen.

card-F03.front: How does Utah law treat freeway U-turns and driving or loading passengers on the shoulder?
card-F03.expected_back: U-turns on the freeway are prohibited, as is driving or stopping for passengers in the emergency lane outside the solid white line.

card-F04.front: What must a left-lane driver do when faster traffic closes from behind, and what penalty looms?
card-F04.expected_back: A left-lane driver approached from behind must move safely right so faster traffic can pass; lingering can draw a citation for impeding.

card-F05.front: Which four vehicle or occupancy groups ride Utah's Interstate fifteen express lanes free of charge?
card-F05.expected_back: Express lanes on I-fifteen are free for vehicles with two or more occupants, plus motorcycles, buses, and registered clean-fuel decal vehicles.

card-F06.front: Where is crossing into or out of Utah's express lane unlawful versus permitted?
card-F06.expected_back: Crossing a double white line to enter or leave the express lane is prohibited; enter or exit only at dotted-line access points.

card-F07.front: How many vehicles may proceed per green on a ramp meter, and when do meters apply?
card-F07.expected_back: Ramp meters show alternating red and green and generally release one vehicle per green; obey only when the meter-on sign is lit.

card-F08.front: Who may use a runaway-vehicle ramp, and what parking rules apply along its approach?
card-F08.expected_back: Runaway-vehicle ramps are for emergency stops only; stopping, standing, or parking on or in the path of one is prohibited.

card-F09.front: When is an off-ramp turnaround back onto the freeway legal at a single-point interchange?
card-F09.expected_back: A U-turn from the off-ramp that re-enters the freeway at a single-point interchange is allowed only when facing a green arrow; finish once started.

card-F10.front: What should you scan for while slowing at an intersection, and what assumption must you avoid?
card-F10.expected_back: At every intersection slow, scan for controls, cross traffic, walkers, riders, and sight blocks, and never assume others will yield.

card-F11.front: Where do you halt at intersection controls, and how much room belongs behind a stopped car?
card-F11.expected_back: Stop fully behind signs, signals, walks, or stop lines; when queued, leave room to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead.

card-F12.front: How do broken yellow center lines differ from solid or double yellow lines for passing?
card-F12.expected_back: Broken yellow center lines permit passing when safe; solid lines and double-center lines restrict or bar passing as marked.

card-F13.front: Where must you stop at controlled corners, and which crosswalk pedestrians hold passage rights?
card-F13.expected_back: Stop behind the stop line or crosswalk at signs and signals and grant passage to anyone in or entering any crosswalk, marked or not.

card-F14.front: What three checks precede entering a shared center turn lane, and what distance cap normally applies?
card-F14.expected_back: Before entering a shared center lane for a left turn, check mirrors, signal left and check the left blind spot. Entry is limited to five hundred feet before the turn, except when the last car is farther than five hundred feet from the intersection.

card-F15.front: What default Utah speed limits apply in active school zones, business or residential streets, and major highways?
card-F15.expected_back: Default limits absent signs or hazards are twenty near schools during recess or arrival and dismissal, twenty-five in business and residential areas, and fifty-five on major highways as posted.

card-F16.front: At which road features and visibility conditions must you drop below normal cruising speed?
card-F16.expected_back: Reduce speed at intersections, rail crossings, curves, hill crests, narrow or winding roads, work zones, and whenever sight or control is reduced.

card-F17.front: What four-step sequence takes you safely into and out of a roundabout?
card-F17.expected_back: Roundabout routine is slow on approach, yield to traffic inside and to walkers, enter when clear, then exit at the wanted street.

card-F18.front: How does a steady yellow traffic signal differ in meaning from a flashing yellow signal?
card-F18.expected_back: Steady yellow means the signal is about to turn red; flashing yellow means slow, proceed with care, and be ready to stop.

card-F19.front: Who holds the green light when you face a flashing yellow turn arrow, and what must you do?
card-F19.expected_back: Flashing yellow arrow permits the turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and walkers, who hold the green.

card-F20.front: How does turning right on a circular red light differ from facing a lighted red arrow?
card-F20.expected_back: Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless posted otherwise; right or left on a red arrow requires waiting for a go indication.

card-F21.front: How should you clear railroad tracks, and when may you proceed after crossing gates activate?
card-F21.expected_back: Cross rail tracks promptly without stopping on them; if gates and lights operate, wait until arms rise and lights end before going.

card-F22.front: How do standard warning signs compare in shape and color with highway guide signs?
card-F22.expected_back: Warning signs are generally diamond-shaped yellow with black symbols; guide signs are square or rectangular green, brown, or blue.

card-F23.front: What colors and shapes mark Utah work-zone signs, and what penalty hits work-zone speeders?
card-F23.expected_back: Work-zone signs are diamond or rectangular orange with black legends; speeding fines in work zones are doubled.

card-F24.front: Who receives right-of-way for cars inside intersections, left turns, tied four-way stops, and driveway exits?
card-F24.expected_back: Grant the way to the vehicle already in the intersection, to oncoming traffic on a left turn, to the driver on the right at a tied four-way stop, and to road traffic when leaving a drive.

card-R09-01.front: What do a green arrow and a red X overhead indicate above a reversible flex lane?
card-R09-01.expected_back: Flex-lane use follows overhead signal; green arrow open, red X closed

card-R09-02.front: Besides keeping your following gap, which three maneuvers are strictly barred on Utah freeways?
card-R09-02.memory_hook: Keep gap, no U-turn, shoulder, ramp-back
card-R09-02.expected_back: Freeway: keep following gap, no U-turn, no emergency-lane driving, no ramp reversal

card-R09-03.front: Why must a vehicle in the left lane shift right when another driver approaches from behind?
card-R09-03.expected_back: Left-lane vehicle approached from behind must move right to avoid impeding

card-R09-04.front: What occupancy or pass requirement and pavement-stripe rule govern entering Utah's express lane?
card-R09-04.expected_back: Express lane needs qualifying occupancy; double white line crossing barred except at dotted access points

card-R09-05.front: How can a solo driver legally use the express lane, and how does clean-fuel authorization work?
card-R09-05.expected_back: Single-occupant use needs paid pass account; clean-fuel decal is separate windshield authorization

card-R09-06.front: How should you use acceleration lanes, freeway exits, and active ramp meters?
card-R09-06.expected_back: Use acceleration lane to match speed; exit early and steady; metered ramp admits one vehicle per green

card-R09-07.front: Compare stopping rules on runaway-vehicle ramps against single-point interchange off-ramp U-turns?
card-R09-07.expected_back: Runaway ramp emergency-only with no stopping; SPUI off-ramp U-turn allowed on green arrow, never stop mid-crossing

card-R09-08.front: What ordered sequence guides approaching, checking, crossing, and clearing an intersection?
card-R09-08.expected_back: Approach slow and scan; stop behind line; look left-right-left; cross without lane change; then merge right

card-R09-09.front: How do continuous-flow, diverging-diamond, and thru-U-turn interchanges handle left turns?
card-R09-09.expected_back: Continuous-flow, diverging-diamond and thru-U-turn each redirect lefts; follow staged signals and lane guides

card-R09-10.front: How do yellow and white lines divide traffic, and what crosswalk and center-lane duties apply?
card-R09-10.expected_back: Yellow divides opposing flow; white divides same-direction flow; stop behind line and yield in crosswalk; shared center lane entry limited

card-R09-11.front: How does Utah's reasonable-and-prudent speed law treat hazards as well as driving way too slowly?
card-R09-11.expected_back: Basic law is reasonable-and-prudent; posted defaults by area; slow for hazards; too-slow impeding is citable

card-R09-12.front: Compare green ball, green arrow, steady yellow, and flashing yellow traffic indications?
card-R09-12.expected_back: Green go-if-clear; green arrow only-arrow-direction after yielding; yellow about-to-red; flashing yellow caution

card-R09-13.front: How do steady red, flashing red, red arrows, dead signals, and live police officers interact?
card-R09-13.expected_back: Red stop-and-wait; right-on-red after stop unless barred; flashing red stop-then-go; red arrows stop; officer overrides signal; dead signal stop-first

card-R09-14.front: How do guide, railroad, regulatory, yellow diamond, and orange flagger zones direct drivers?
card-R09-14.expected_back: Guide signs provide directions and service information. Railroad signs call for looking, listening and stopping when required; regulatory signs direct traffic, and yellow diamond signs warn of danger. Work-zone signs use orange backgrounds, speeding fines there are doubled, and a flagger's directions must be obeyed.

card-R09-15.front: Across intersections, left turns, four-way ties, driveways, ramps, and crosswalks, who yields right-of-way?
card-R09-15.expected_back: Assess safety instead of assuming priority. Yield to an earlier arrival at the intersection, to oncoming drivers when turning left, and to the driver on the right when both reach a four-way stop together. A driver leaving a driveway or private road yields to public-road traffic; an entrance-ramp driver yields to interstate traffic. Also yield to people, bicyclists and others remaining in the intersection.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How much alcohol may an alcohol-restricted driver have in the body while operating after an alcohol case?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: An alcohol restricted driver is barred from operating with any alcohol in the body following an alcohol-related conviction, suspension or revocation.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which vehicles may an interlock-restricted driver operate, and how does the device work?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: An interlock restricted driver may operate only a vehicle fitted with an ignition interlock system, which is a constant monitor requiring a breath sample to start and run the vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Which three situations cause Utah to cancel a previously granted driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Cancellation ends a license granted through error or fraud, after application for another state credential, or after required consent is withdrawn.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: How do revocation, suspension, denial, and disqualification each affect driving privileges in Utah?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Revocation ends the privilege to drive, suspension withdraws it temporarily, denial withholds driving privilege, and disqualification withdraws commercial privilege temporarily or permanently.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which three alcohol or controlled-substance combinations meet Utah's extreme driving-under-the-influence definition?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Extreme DUI includes breath or blood alcohol at or above the stated higher threshold, or the lower alcohol threshold combined with measurable controlled substance, or two or more non-excepted controlled substances.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which two patterns of moving violations and cabin distractions count as careless driving in Utah?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Careless driving covers committing two or more moving violations in one continuous drive, or one moving violation while distracted by an in-vehicle non-driving activity such as looking for an object or personal grooming.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How does Utah define vehicle blind spots compared with performing a proper head check?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Blind spots are roadway areas not visible in mirrors during operation, while head checks mean turning the head and looking over the shoulder toward the intended movement.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which vehicle weights, passenger capacities, trailer setups, and cargo types require a commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: A commercial license covers vehicles at or above the stated heavy weight threshold, vehicles built for the stated larger passenger count, plus hazardous materials, doubles or triples, tankers and school buses.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: What defines a Utah low-speed vehicle by wheels, power, speed, seating, and excluded machines?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle is a four-wheeled electric vehicle capped at the stated low maximum speed and four occupants including the driver, excluding golf carts and off-highway vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which four physical features define a personal motorized mobility device under Utah rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A personal motorized mobility device has two non-tandem ground wheels, steering and stopping under normal use, a motor capped at the stated small power limit, and a standing deck.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What intersection shape defines a roundabout, and which direction does traffic circulate?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: A roundabout is a circular intersection with counterclockwise flow.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Who receives a provisional driver license instead of a regular adult license in Utah?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: A provisional license is a Utah license issued to a person under the stated younger-adult age threshold.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: How long can a Utah temporary license grant driving privileges, and which cardholders cannot receive one?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: A temporary license allows driving privileges up to the stated half-year period and is unavailable to driving privilege card holders.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How do Utah rules define Division, operator, and highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Division means the Driver License Division of the Department of Public Safety, operator means a person in actual physical control, and highway means the full width between property lines available for vehicular travel.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Who retains full operating responsibility when modern driver-assist technology is switched on?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Driver-assist features only aid the driver and never assume responsibility for operating the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Which two convenience aids must remain switched off throughout your Utah driving skills exam?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Parking assist and cruise control aids must not be used during the driving skills test.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: What four upkeep and engagement habits must drivers follow on cars equipped with assist tech?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Drivers must stay engaged, consult the owner manual, know system limits, and keep sensors clean and software current.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Which vehicles must carry working brakes on every wheel, and which heavy rig gets a front-wheel exception?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Every motor vehicle needs compliant brakes on all wheels, except a truck or truck tractor with three or more axles may omit front-wheel brakes.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: How should you work an anti-lock brake pedal when stopping on a slick road?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes on a slick surface, hold steady firm pressure instead of pumping the pedal.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: How must skills-test applicants set parking-assist and cruise-control features on exam day?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Skills-test drivers must leave parking assist and cruise control off

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Can electronic driver-assistance features ever substitute for your own eyes and attention?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Assistance systems only support the driver, never replace attention

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: At what minimum width do buses, RVs, and trailers need amber front and red rear clearance lamps visible five hundred feet?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: A bus, RV, or trailer at least eighty inches wide needs two amber front clearance lamps plus side lamps and two red rear lamps, all seen from five hundred feet at night.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: When cargo sticks four feet or more past the bed, how must you mark it by day and at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: A load reaching four feet or more past the bed or body needs two rear flags by day at least twelve inches square, or lamps seen from five hundred feet at night.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What roadside warning kit must trucks, tractors, and buses carry, and what sightline and burn specs apply?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Trucks, truck tractors, and buses carry three flares or red emergency reflectors or lights plus two red flags, seen and distinguished from six hundred feet, with flares burning for twelve hours.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Excluding motorcycles, how many white headlights are required and how far must high and low beams reach?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Except motorcycles, each vehicle needs two white headlights reaching three hundred fifty feet on high beam and one hundred feet on low beam, plus a high-beam indicator.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: From what distances must your horn be audible and your rear license plate readable under its white lamp?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: Every motor vehicle needs a working horn heard from two hundred feet, and every vehicle needs a white plate lamp making the plate readable from fifty feet.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: Which three groups of vehicles and trailers must wear mud flaps or splash guards in Utah?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Mud flaps or guards are required on vehicles rated ten thousand five hundred pounds or more, altered-suspension or altered-tire vehicles, and trailers unladen at seven hundred fifty pounds or more.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: Which fleets are authorized to display red or blue lights visible from the front of the vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: Red or blue light seen from the front is reserved for emergency, school, snow-removal, or otherwise authorized vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: What colors, night visibility distance, and mounting height band apply to side vehicle reflectors?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Each vehicle needs an amber side reflector near the front and a red one near the rear, seen from five hundred feet at night and mounted fifteen to sixty inches high.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: From how many feet away in bright daylight must rear tail-and-stop lamps versus turn signals be visible?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Vehicles need two red rear tail and stop lamps seen from five hundred feet in daylight, and turn signals seen from one hundred feet in normal sunlight.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: What working wiper count and speed-setting rules apply to vehicles with windshields?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: All windshield vehicles need at least one working wiper, both wipers when factory-fitted with two, and multi-speed wipers on models built after nineteen sixty-seven.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: Detail the exact front, side, and rear clearance-lamp colors and night visibility range for vehicles eighty inches or wider?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: For buses, recreational vehicles and trailers at least eighty inches wide, clearance lighting includes two amber front lamps and an amber lamp on each side, plus two red rear lamps and a red lamp on each side toward the rear. These lamps must be visible at night from five hundred feet.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How are non-motorcycle headlights arranged, and what beam distances must high and low settings cover?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Except for motorcycles, a vehicle needs at least two working white headlights, with one on either side. High beams must reach three hundred fifty feet, and low beams one hundred feet.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: How many red tail-and-stop lamps seen at five hundred feet are standard, and which vehicles may run just one?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: Two red tail and stop lamps belong at the rear, visible in ordinary sunlight from five hundred feet behind. Motorcycles and certain vehicles built before nineteen fifty-six may instead have one tail and stop lamp.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Which colors are lawful for front versus rear turn signals, and which vintage narrow cars need none?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Rear turn signals consist of two lamps colored red, yellow or amber; the two front lamps may be white, yellow or amber. They must be visible in normal sunlight from one hundred feet. Vehicles built before nineteen fifty-three need no turn signals if their width is less than eighty inches.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: How many hours of classroom teaching are required in a Utah high-school driver education course?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Utah high-school classroom driver education requires twenty-seven hours of classroom teaching.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: How many classroom instruction hours are required in a Utah commercial or private-school course?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: A commercial or private-school classroom course requires eighteen hours of instruction.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How many study hours must an approved Utah online or home-study driver education course include?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: An approved online or home-study course requires thirty hours of study.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: How many behind-the-wheel hours are mandatory in driver education, and how is six-hour observation treated?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Driver education requires six hours of driving instruction behind the wheel. A school may also require six hours of observation by a licensed instructor.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What two conditions must an out-of-state driver education certificate satisfy for credit in Utah?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Out-of-state certificates must meet Utah hour totals and include a completed DLD200 form.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Does Utah accept out-of-state online or home-study driver education completion certificates?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Out-of-state online or home-study certificates are not accepted in Utah.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What schooling and logged parent-supervised driving hours must applicants aged fifteen through eighteen complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Applicants aged fifteen through eighteen must finish driver education and log forty hours with a parent or guardian, including ten after sunset.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What two ways can an unlicensed adult aged nineteen or older qualify for a Utah license?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Adults nineteen or older without a license may qualify after holding a learner permit for ninety days with forty hours of driving including ten after sunset, or by finishing driver education to waive the wait.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Who may ride beside a Class D learner under eighteen, and when can another adult twenty-one-plus substitute?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: For a Class D learner under eighteen, the adjacent front-seat supervisor must be an approved instructor, a licensed parent or legal guardian, or the licensed adult who signed the permit. Another licensed adult, at least twenty-one and neither parent nor guardian, qualifies only if the parent or guardian is unlicensed and the adult carries their note or other proof allowing that supervision.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Which night curfew and six-month passenger rules govern a sixteen-year-old driver, and where do exceptions differ?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: For a licensed sixteen-year-old, driving is restricted between midnight and five in the morning. Exceptions are a licensed driver aged twenty-one in the front seat, an agricultural assignment, travel to or from work or a school-sponsored activity, or an emergency. For the first six months after license issuance, passengers must be immediate family; that restriction has exceptions for the same adult accompaniment, agricultural assignments and emergencies, but not work or school travel.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How many total and after-sunset parent-supervised hours pair with driver education at ages fifteen to eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Drivers aged fifteen to eighteen must finish approved driver education and log forty hours with a parent or guardian, with ten hours after sunset

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How can an applicant nineteen or older qualify without taking formal driver education?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Drivers nineteen or older may skip driver education by holding a learner permit ninety days and logging forty hours with ten hours after sunset

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What age, tests, and visit steps earn an initial Utah learner permit, and how long does it last?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: An entry-level learner permit requires an appointment with documents and fee, a passed knowledge test and eye test, a minimum age of fifteen, and it stays valid for eighteen months while the permit stays on hand.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What age, schooling, holding periods, and test-score freshness govern Utah's six-month renewal permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: A six-month renewal permit needs a minimum age of sixteen, driver education completion, six months of holding for teens and ninety days for adults, possession on hand, and scores valid for twelve months.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What dollar fees apply to a Utah learner permit, provisional license, regular license, duplicate, and driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Listed fees include nineteen for a learner permit, thirty-nine for a provisional license, fifty-two for a regular license and renewal, twenty-three for a duplicate, and eight for a driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How do Utah's required study hours compare across high school, private commercial school, and online home study?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Utah classroom hours are twenty-seven for high school, eighteen for commercial or private school, and thirty for approved online or home study

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does Utah separate mandatory behind-the-wheel hours from six hours of instructor observation?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The driving-instruction requirement is six hours behind the wheel. Six hours of observation by a licensed instructor may also be required by the school.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Where must your learner permit stay while driving, and what status must your front-seat supervisor hold?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: A learner permit stays in immediate possession while driving and the front-seat supervisor must be a licensed driver

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How long must learner permits be held at sixteen or seventeen, at eighteen with driver ed, and at nineteen-plus?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Holding periods are six months at age sixteen or seventeen, none at age eighteen with driver education, and ninety days at age nineteen or older

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: How should your back, feet, and legs fit the driver's seat before shifting out of park?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Slouching or stretching on tiptoes delays emergency brake force and tires your lower back on long Utah drives.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: How far should your chest sit from the steering wheel, and how high should the wheel top sit?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Keeping roughly 10 inches to the airbag hub with the wheel rim at or below shoulder and chin height prevents deployment injury.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Where should the headrest touch your head, and how should your foot move between the gas and brake?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Setting the headrest above ear height stops whiplash, while pivoting on a grounded heel smooths pedal transitions.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: What posture and chest-to-wheel measurement protect you best in the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Sitting tall against the backrest with ten inches of airbag clearance balances steering leverage with crash protection.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Relative to your shoulders and chin, how high should the top of the steering wheel be adjusted?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Tilting the rim lower aims the airbag toward your chest bone instead of upward into your chin and face.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How high on the back of your head should a properly adjusted headrest make contact?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: A low headrest acts like a fulcrum in a rear-end hit, whereas contact above the ears catches your skull squarely.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How do you aim the inside rearview mirror and adapt it for daytime versus nighttime glare?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Centering the entire rear window and flipping the night anti-glare tab keeps trailing traffic visible without blinding beams.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How much of your own car's side should appear in properly aimed outside mirrors?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Filling side mirrors with your own doors wastes outward view and leaves wide adjacent-lane blind spots.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How do the inside mirror and two outside mirrors work together when adjusted properly?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Framing the rear glass centered inside while pushing side mirrors outward creates overlapping rear-to-side lane coverage.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Who must use a seat belt or child restraint, and what three protections do belts provide?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Belts keep passengers inside the cabin shell, absorb impact energy, and hold the driver behind the wheel to steer.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Where must the shoulder strap and lap belt rest on your body, and what two shortcuts are unsafe?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Tucking the strap under an arm or behind your back concentrates crash loads onto ribs or your soft abdomen.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What does Utah's occupant-restraint law mandate for all passengers and for children age eight or younger?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Adult belts ride dangerously high on small frames, so Utah requires car or booster seats through age eight.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: How many pounds of crash force hit a 150-pound person in a 30 mph impact, and why can't arms brace against it?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Multiplying 150 pounds by 30 mph produces 4,500 pounds, over two tons of force no human arms can hold back.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: How are unbuckled-passenger citations counted for a Utah driver, and when does special stop authority kick in?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Three unbuckled passengers can mean three separate tickets, and anyone under 16 unrestrained triggers primary stop authority.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Where do lap and shoulder straps belong, and where must the shoulder strap never be routed?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Strong pelvic and collarbone structures absorb crash forces safely only when neither strap is slipped behind or under.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: At what height may a child age eight or younger graduate out of an approved safety or booster seat in Utah?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Four feet nine inches, or 57 inches, is Utah's statutory height benchmark where vehicle belts finally fit young hips and shoulders.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What age, weight, and height milestones guide moving a child from rear-facing to forward-facing to a booster?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Keep toddlers rear-facing to 2 and 30 pounds, harnessed to 4 and 40 pounds, and boosted to 57 inches.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How must children ages eight through twelve be restrained, and through what age should kids stay in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Keeping everyone 12 and younger buckled in the rear row shields growing bodies from front-seat dashboard airbags.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How fast do dashboard airbags inflate, and how do they interact with seat belts?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Deploying at up to 200 mph, airbags injure unbuckled riders thrown forward and work safely only alongside fastened belts.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What strict rule governs infants and passenger airbags, and what if an older child must ride in an airbag seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: An active passenger airbag strikes a rear-facing infant shell with lethal force; if unavoidable for older kids, push the seat fully back.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What offense classes apply in Utah to disabling an airbag versus smoking in a car carrying children 15 or younger?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Know both Utah penalties cold because airbag tampering or non-repair is a Class B misdemeanor while smoking near kids 15-and-under is an infraction.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Which young passengers require an approved safety seat unless they reach 57 inches?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Remember both halves of Utah's booster rule covering children eight or younger until reaching 57 inches tall.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Until what minimum age and weight should a young child remain rear-facing in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Cradling a toddler's heavy head and fragile neck rear-facing requires reaching both age two and thirty pounds.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Until what minimum age and weight should a child ride forward-facing in a five-point harness in the back seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Five-point harnesses spread crash loads across shoulders and hips until the child hits at least age four and forty pounds.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Once a child outgrows a 40-pound harness, how long must they keep riding in a belt-positioning booster?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Boosters lift children around 40 pounds up until the adult belt sits properly at 57 inches tall.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: How should every driver treat airbags alongside seat belts and infant carriers?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Respect airbags as explosive supplemental cushions requiring buckled belts and keeping infants strictly out of the front seat.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: How should your hands grip the steering wheel, and which way do you turn it moving forward or backward?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Gripping the outer rim with fingers instead of palms gives smooth feel while steering whichever way you want the car to go.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What gear, pedal, and instrument checks belong right before putting your vehicle in motion?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Starting with Park or depressed clutch plus firm foot brake prevents lurching while you verify warning lamps and gauges.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How should you position your body and steer when backing up, and on which highways is reversing illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Draping your right arm over the passenger seat to look directly through the rear glass beats mirrors, and freeway backing is forbidden.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: For how many seconds must you signal before turning or changing lanes, and what curb moves also require signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Memorize Utah's signature 2-second minimum blinker rule before every turn, lane shift, or pull to or from a curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: What four-step sequence completes a safe lane change in Utah?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Checking mirrors, flashing for two full seconds, glancing over your shoulder, and cancelling after merging eliminates side-swipes.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: How must you manage lane lines during ordinary travel, turns, and crossing intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Drifting into a wider exit lane mid-turn or changing lanes inside an intersection surprises drivers turning beside you.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a highway merge, and what painted triangle is off-limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Through-lane traffic owns priority, and cutting across the solid-white gore triangle risks hitting attenuators or fast cars.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: How does the zipper method work when heavy traffic approaches a lane-ending merge point?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Using both lanes all the way to the taper and alternating one-for-one cuts backup length and road friction.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: How much clearance from oncoming traffic must remain when returning right after a pass, and what right-pass rule applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Cutting back with less than 200 feet to spare forces oncoming panic stops, and driving off pavement to pass right is illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Alongside hills, curves, intersections, rails, and bridges, what snowplow situations ban passing in Utah?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Utah adds vital winter rules barring passes on a plow's deployed-blade side or past snowplows staggered in echelon.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What sight-distance rule and three roadway locations prohibit making a U-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Turning completely around requires 500 feet of clear view both ways and is barred at no-U signs, tracks, and freeways.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R05.question_text: At least how many feet clear of approaching oncoming traffic must you finish returning to the right lane?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R05.teaching_text: At highway speeds two opposing cars close 200 feet in roughly one second, making that buffer an absolute floor.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R06.question_text: What two passing bans apply around snowplows operating with flashing yellow lights?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R06.teaching_text: Wing blades throw heavy ice chunks wide while three or more staggered plows sweep the entire highway width together.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R09.question_text: How does a forward two-point turn differ from a reverse two-point turn using a driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R09.teaching_text: Backing into a clear side driveway lets you drive out nose-first with full sightlines instead of backing into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R10.question_text: Where is a three-point turn appropriate, and where are U-turns strictly barred?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R10.teaching_text: Save three-point turns strictly for quiet narrow two-lane roads and skip U-turns on hills, curves, tracks, freeways, or short sightlines.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R11.question_text: In what exact order do mirrors, two-second signal, shoulder check, and signal cancel happen on a lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R11.teaching_text: Running that exact four-step checklist every time impresses road-test examiners and catches bikes tucked in blind spots.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R12.question_text: How do normal merge yielding, solid-white gore lines, and jammed zipper merges fit together?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R12.teaching_text: Yield to open freeway flow without crossing gore paint, and fill both lanes taking turns when traffic backs up.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Where do you halt at a stop sign or light, and what visual cue sets safe spacing behind a stopped car?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Stopping where you still see the lead car's rear tires touching asphalt leaves room to steer around a stall.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What complete sequence secures a vehicle parked facing downhill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Turning front tires toward the curb until one touches chocks the car immediately before shifting to Park and setting the brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Which way do front wheels point when parking uphill with a curb versus uphill with no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: With a curb, turning left catches the back of the front tire; without a curb, turning right rolls runaways off-road.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb must a parked vehicle sit, and what three shutdown steps apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Tucking inside 12 inches while stopping the motor, setting the parking brake, and locking doors keeps lanes clear and cars secure.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Within what distance window from the nearest rail must you stop at an active or stop-controlled railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Halting more than 15 feet back clears overhanging boxcars while staying within 50 feet keeps crossing sightlines sharp.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: On which two roadway layouts do both directions stop for red school-bus lights, and on which two do opposing lanes continue?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Utah's exam loves testing that opposing lanes keep moving on median-divided four-plus roads AND five-lane center-turn roads.
sec08-card-sec08-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Undivided two-four stop, median five-turn go

visual_sync.text_span: Undivided two-four stop, median five-turn go

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R01.question_text: Beside a raised curb, how do downhill versus uphill front-wheel angles oppose each other?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R01.teaching_text: Gravity pulls opposite ways on the two grades, so point downhill tires into the concrete and uphill tires away.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R02.question_text: Which way must you steer your front tires when parking uphill along a road shoulder without a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R02.teaching_text: With no raised curb to catch a left-turned tire, pointing toward the right edge steers any rollaway off traffic lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R03.question_text: How close to the curb must your rear tire and finished parallel-parking position rest?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R03.teaching_text: Leaving a wheel more than one foot, or 12 inches, out into the street fails road-test parallel parking.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R04.question_text: What no-parking distances apply in Utah near fire hydrants, crosswalks, signs or signals, and railroad rails?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R04.teaching_text: Lock in Utah's ascending stair-step sequence of 15 at hydrants, 20 at crosswalks, 30 at signals, and 50 at rails.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R07.question_text: How do median dividers or a five-lane shared center turn lane change oncoming school-bus stopping duties?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R07.teaching_text: Both directions halt on two-lane or undivided four-lane roads, whereas divided highways and five-lane center-turn corridors stop same-way only.

sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R08.question_text: Between what minimum and maximum distances from the nearest rail must you stop at a controlled crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-basic-driving-R08.teaching_text: Stopping inside that 15-to-50-foot safety window keeps your hood clear of passing trains at gates, lights, watchmen, or stop signs.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What immediate action is legally required of every driver involved in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Rolling away even briefly turns an ordinary collision into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: How long can Utah suspend or revoke your license for leaving a crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Fleeing a collision risks losing your driving privilege through suspension or revocation for up to twelve months.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: What maximum jail term and dollar fine can follow leaving a Utah crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Beyond license loss, leaving a crash scene exposes you to a year jailed or twenty-five hundred dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What two duties do involved drivers owe anyone injured in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Calling emergency medical transport and rendering reasonable help fulfills your legal duty to injured crash victims.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Which three crash outcomes require calling law enforcement immediately in Utah?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Skipping an immediate police report when combined damage hits twenty-five hundred dollars violates Utah crash law.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Which four pieces of driver, vehicle, and policy information must crash participants exchange?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Leaving without sharing your registration number and insurer contact details alongside name and address is incomplete.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How long must an involved driver remain after halting at a crash scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Stopping briefly without completing aid and information exchange still carries severe hit-and-run penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: When only property is damaged, may you move your car out of traffic before exchanging details?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Pulling onto a nearby shoulder prevents secondary pileups without excusing your duty to remain and exchange papers.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What three crash triggers require immediate law-enforcement notification rather than private exchange alone?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Private fender-bender swaps apply only when nobody is hurt and damage stays below Utah's reporting threshold.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: During what afternoon hours do most crashes cluster, and what share involves driver error?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Commuter rush and school dismissal combine with human mistakes across three out of every four crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: How should you apply the parking brake if regular brakes fail, and why stay ready?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Yanking the parking brake hard locks rear wheels into an uncontrollable spin unless applied gradually.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How do you brake hard with antilock brakes when the pedal vibrates and clicks?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Pumping or lifting off when antilock pedals chatter defeats computer wheel-lock prevention and lengthens stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Which four visibility steps protect a disabled car, including exact flare distance behind it?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Setting warning flares two hundred to three hundred feet back gives highway traffic stopping distance.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Along with flashers, raised hood, marker cloth, and rear warning devices, what completes breakdown safety?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Making your stalled car unmistakable from far behind protects everyone while roadside assistance responds.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How does emergency braking and steering with antilock brakes differ from a non-equipped vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Antilock systems let you steer around hazards under full pedal pressure while older brakes follow manual technique.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: What criminal misdemeanor class and credential losses hit a driver operating without required security?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Driving uninsured in Utah brings a Class B misdemeanor alongside losing both your license and registration.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: After how many days does an unpaid crash judgment suspend driving privileges, and what restores them?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Letting a court crash judgment sit unpaid past sixty days suspends your license until paid with future proof.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: How many years must required future financial-responsibility proof normally remain on file?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Canceling required future-proof insurance early before completing three full years immediately re-triggers license suspension.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Which two Utah coverages are mandatory by law, and who typically requires collision and comprehensive?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: State law mandates liability and personal-injury no-fault coverage while auto lenders demand collision and comprehensive.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Beyond a misdemeanor charge, which three items can operating without owner security cost until settled?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Operating without required owner security can strip your license, registration, and physical plates until proof and fees clear.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: What two steps lift a license suspension caused by an unsatisfied crash-damage judgment?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Paying the damage award alone is not enough until future-proof insurance is also filed.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How do Utah's two legally required coverages separate from uninsured-motorist, collision, and comprehensive policies?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Exam questions mix mandatory liability and no-fault medical protection with uninsured-motorist, crash collision, and non-crash comprehensive.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Which three Utah credentials allow a state resident to drive legally on a public roadway?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Once Utah residency attaches, driving on public streets requires holding an active Utah credential.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which five actions classify someone as a Utah resident for driver-licensing purposes?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Claiming resident tuition, taking permanent Utah work, registering locally, or staying six months triggers residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Does spending six months in Utah within a single calendar year establish licensing residency by itself?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Even without changing jobs or voter records, six months inside one calendar year requires Utah licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Which two everyday living milestones immediately make someone a Utah resident for licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Moving in permanently or spending half a calendar year in Utah triggers resident licensing duties.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: What must every Utah resident carry to operate a motor vehicle on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Driving on public streets as a resident without an active Utah license or permit is unlawful.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: At what minimum age may a nonresident drive in Utah using a valid home-state or foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Visitors under sixteen cannot drive in Utah even if another jurisdiction issued them an early credential.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which temporarily assigned workers and military households may keep driving on valid out-of-state or foreign licenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Temporary employer, religious, private, government, or active-duty military postings allow keeping valid outside licenses.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Which age, record, exam, warrant, residency, or teen-training gaps block someone from getting a Utah license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Out-of-state suspensions, open warrants, failed exams, nonresidency, or missing teen permit months block issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Which three types of construction or farm machines need no driver license on Utah highways during work?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Active construction or agricultural work exempts road rollers, highway machinery, and farm tractors from licensure.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Up to how long may a visitor drive in Utah on a valid out-of-state or foreign license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Crossing six months in Utah ends visitor driving privileges and triggers state residency rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How many federally compliant star-marked credentials may one person hold across states at the same time?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Holding a compliant Utah license forbids keeping a second compliant identification card from another state.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: What minimum age and maximum stay govern a licensed visitor driving in Utah?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Test questions pair the sixteen-year minimum visitor age directly with Utah's six-month driving limit.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Which basic age cutoff and privilege status immediately disqualify a Utah license applicant?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Being younger than sixteen or carrying a denied driving status stops a Utah application cold.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Which two interstate compacts include Utah, and what does the forty-five-state plus District of Columbia compact share?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Out-of-state tickets follow you back to Utah through forty-five member states and Washington.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Which states stay outside each interstate compact, and what happens when an out-of-state citation goes unanswered?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Ignoring a ticket in any of forty-four violator-compact states suspends your home license until settled.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What information does the Driver License Compact share, and how many states remain outside it?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Forty-five states send conviction records home while only five nonmember states stay outside.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: What does the Non-Resident Violator Compact forward, and how many states remain outside it?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Unanswered out-of-state tickets get forwarded home across forty-four member states while six remain nonmembers.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What minimum age and personal-vehicle weight ceiling apply to a regular Utah Class D license?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Personal vehicles above twenty-six thousand pounds step outside standard Class D licensing scope.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What prerequisite applies under age nineteen, and how are Class D holders under twenty-one classified?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Drivers under twenty-one hold provisional Class D status tracked under a stricter separate point system.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: How do Utah Classes A, B, C, and D separate vehicles by weight, towed units, cargo, and minimum age?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Classes A and B allow intrastate driving at eighteen to twenty while Class C hazmat requires twenty-one.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: Which two core limits define the Utah Class D scope grouping?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Remembering minimum age sixteen alongside the twenty-six-thousand-pound cap anchors every Class D question.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: What primary measurement groups commercial Classes A, B, and C together?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Single and towed combined-weight cutoffs determine whether a rig falls into Class A, B, or C.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: Which three specialized hauling or transport uses are grouped under endorsement codes?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Endorsement letters authorize extra high-risk cargo or passenger roles on top of your base class.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Which three operating areas do Utah license restriction codes narrow down?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Unlike endorsements adding uses, restriction codes cap equipment, road speed, or medical driving conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How does eligibility differ between a Utah limited-term credential and a driving privilege card?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Non-citizens with compliant lawful status get limited-term cards while ineligible lawful residents and undocumented applicants use privilege cards.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Which identity documents qualify for a regular Class D or identification card, and which birth records get rejected?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Bringing a hospital souvenir, wallet-sized, laminated, or photocopied birth certificate gets turned away at check-in.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Which documents satisfy Utah's Social Security requirement if you lack a signed government card?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Tax wage forms, a pay stub, or a lawful-presence agency ineligibility letter substitute for a missing signed card.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: How many Utah address documents are needed, how recent must they be, and which records qualify?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Bank, utility, credit-card, tax, lease, court, transcript, or title papers older than ninety days fail residency review.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: Which three proof categories combine to form Utah's core licensing document triad?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Bringing identity and address proofs without required driving-experience verification leaves a first license incomplete.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What proves driving experience for a first Utah license, and which two credentials skip it?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Learner permits and identification cards skip experience proof, whereas first licenses require teen driver ed or prior licensure.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Which two unexpired, electronically verified document options establish limited-term identity and lawful status?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Both an unexpired federal work authorization card and a foreign passport with visa and arrival record undergo verification.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: What rules govern photocopies and name mismatches at the licensing counter, and what does a bounced check cost?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Faxes and photocopies fail immediately, name changes need legal proof, and bounced checks add twenty dollars.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Which layered identity records, tax proof, and fingerprint item are required for an original driving privilege card?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Original privilege-card applicants pair translated foreign primary and secondary proofs with tax numbers and sealed fingerprints.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: Can a driving privilege card verify age or identity, when does it expire, and can you drive before mail delivery?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: No temporary paper permit issues, so driving before your yearly-expiring plastic privilege card arrives is illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: When do original adult over-twenty-one licenses expire compared with under-twenty-one provisional licenses?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Both credentials expire on your birthday, spanning eight years over twenty-one versus five years under twenty-one.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How does Utah treat six-month visitor licenses, out-of-state learner permits, and old licenses upon Utah application?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Out-of-state learner permits never authorize Utah driving, and full outside licenses must be surrendered when applying.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: How early may you renew, what qualifies for online good-driver renewal, and how fast must Class D moves report?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Class D address changes require ten-day notice while online renewal caps reportable violations at six in eight years.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: What shared element links Utah renewal, replacement, and address-change responsibilities together?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Tracking early renewal windows and the ten-day move deadline keeps your credential continuously valid.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Who is eligible for a Utah identification card, and may someone hold both a Utah license and identification card?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: State law restricts identification cards to Utah residents and bans holding a driver license alongside one.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Where does Utah's written knowledge test pull its material from, and what does it verify?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Studying the official Utah handbook covers every sampled question checking your grasp of state law and safe habits.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Is Utah's written knowledge test timed, how long does it usually take, and what score passes?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Take an unhurried 30 to 45 minutes reading every choice carefully since there is no countdown clock and 80 percent passes.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How many written knowledge tests may a candidate take in one day, and what follows a failed try?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Busy Driver License Division offices allow a second same-day try only when scheduling permits, otherwise requiring a retest appointment.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How many written-test attempts and months does a single application fee cover?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Missing three times or letting twelve months lapse exhausts your initial fee and requires paying again for three fresh tries.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Which two administrative boundaries pair together to govern written-test retakes in the Utah manual?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Tracking both how many tries you get and when a fresh fee kicks in prevents surprise counter delays.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What additional online exam must first-time Class D applicants pass, and what score is required?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Utah's unique Traffic Safety and Trends exam demands a 100 percent score online, though you may retake it unlimited times.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What topic accounts for half the questions on Utah's Traffic Safety and Trends exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Utah Highway Safety Office fatality statistics drive half the exam so new drivers recognize what actually kills motorists.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How does the minimum age to take the driving-skills exam differ between the DLD and a high school or Third-Party Tester?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: High-school driver ed and Third-Party Testers can administer the road test at 15, whereas DLD offices require age 16.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What basic vehicle condition and cabin-occupant rule apply during the driving-skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Parents, friends, and pets wait outside because only the applicant and examiner ride inside the registered, belted vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which registration, lighting, glass, mirror, door, seat, and brake items are checked before your road test starts?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: A burned-out brake bulb, stuck driver window, missing left mirror, or broken parking brake cancels your road test before moving.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What broad range of habits and maneuvers do examiners grade during Utah's driving-skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Examiners score everything from calm attitude and posture to hill and parallel parking, three-point U-turns, backing, and lane changes.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Which two road-exam topics does the handbook group together when summarizing behind-the-wheel testing?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Knowing both what maneuvers earn deductions and how retest rules work prepares you fully for road-test day.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What practice, daily limit, three-strike fee, and overall completion deadline govern driving-skills tests?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Compare carefully because written fees last 12 months while all testing must wrap up within 6 months of paying.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which seven dangerous or unlawful mistakes trigger automatic failure on the Utah skills exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Breaking a law, missing a yield, bumping a curb, forcing others to swerve, examiner intervention, or extreme speed ends the test.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How does alcohol impair your ability to handle unfamiliar traffic situations?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Alcohol dulls the brain's ability to pull past lessons cleanly when sudden road hazards unfold.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which sense is most vital for driving, and at what blood alcohol mark is it harmed?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Eye tracking and focus degrade at zero point zero two for every driver well before legal limits.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to begin impairing motor-vehicle operation?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Assuming you need multiple drinks before skill drops ignores measurable loss after a single serving.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: When does alcohol harm begin, and what is the safest driving decision after drinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Because impairment starts with drink one, handing off driving completely beats guessing whether you are legal.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Beyond alcohol, which three drug sources and mental state can impair safe driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Pharmacy cold tablets, doctor prescriptions, illicit substances, and intense emotional upset each degrade vehicle control.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Which four driving skills drop from the first drink, making feeling drunk a bad test?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel tipsy misses silent early drops in signal color reading and brake timing.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Why can someone lose sharp eyesight and vehicle control well before appearing intoxicated?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Driving eyesight and steering precision slip after one drink long before slurred speech shows up.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Which three practical steps protect safety when anger, worry, excitement, fear, or sadness strike?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Stepping back to calm down, padding your schedule, or letting someone else drive prevents emotional mistakes.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Which three alcohol actions are completely unlawful for anyone under age twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance rules ban purchasing, possessing, or consuming alcohol anywhere before your twenty-first birthday.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: How long do drivers aged thirteen through twenty lose licenses for first and repeat alcohol acts?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Even teens too young to drive yet face one-year then two-year court license suspensions.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What privilege loss hits an under-twenty-one driver with measurable alcohol on first versus ten-year repeat offenses?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: A second offense within ten years locks out driving for two years or until twenty-one, whichever is longer.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What blood alcohol mark breaks Utah's general driving law versus its commercial-driver threshold?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Utah enforces America's strictest zero point zero five general limit alongside zero point zero four for commercial drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Can an adult twenty-one or older break Utah's alcohol driving law while testing below the general number?
